content:
State estimation is the process of inferring the internal condition (state) of a system from indirect, noisy measurements. In control systems, you rarely have direct access to all the variables that describe the system’s true state, so you estimate them to make informed decisions.

Imagine driving a car in fog: you cannot see the road clearly (measurements are noisy and incomplete), but you still need to estimate your position and speed to steer safely. State estimation combines what you measure with what you expect from the system’s behavior to produce the best guess of the true state.

Why is this essential? Because control actions rely on knowing the current state accurately. Without good state estimates, the controller might react to wrong information, causing poor performance or instability.

Does this example of driving in fog help clarify why state estimation matters?
